A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NeuralFLoC and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C. Content can be matched reliably across layout changes; the appendices are identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original registration and clustering experiments, ablations, sensitivity and robustness analyses, and large-scale results in Sections 5-6 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds joint-method comparisons, an STFT ablation, and empirical cluster-number estimates.

M1.justification: Section 6 introduces a TV-based elbow procedure for selecting an unknown cluster count, replacing Section 3.1's generic validation or sparsity suggestions. The core architecture, losses, and training procedure remain unchanged. The component indices added to Equations 5-6 clarify the existing mixture of cluster-specific flows.

E1.justification: The datasets, domains, perturbation scenarios, and large-scale coverage remain unchanged. Section 6 adds a separate task of recovering an unknown cluster count on the five existing dataset configurations; v1's reported evaluations supply the true count. The main performance benchmarks still use ground-truth counts.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds three previously unevaluated classical joint registration-and-clustering methods: SRC, BSRC, and JPCCA. It also adds the Fourier-to-STFT variant. These substantially broaden the comparison beyond sequential pipelines and existing internal ablations. The large-scale comparator set in Table A.3 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds an STFT replacement control and a separate evaluation using label-free TV elbow selection of the cluster count. Existing sample sizes, ATV/ACC/NMI metrics, ground-truth counts in the main benchmarks, and training budgets remain unchanged. The extra irregular-sampling preprocessing description does not establish that the retained experiment was changed or rerun.

E4.justification: The new STFT ablation tests the importance of the Fourier feature representation, and the cluster-count analysis tests practical selection without known counts. Existing registration/clustering ablations, parameter sensitivity, robustness tests, and appendix case studies are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten repetitions and report means, with paired t-tests over ten seeds in Table A.2. That table and its p-values are identical; no significance test for the new STFT variant or uncertainty analysis for cluster-count selection is added.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially expands comparative results with SRC, BSRC, JPCCA, and STFT scores across all five configurations. For example, their Shapes ACC values are 0.807, 0.755, 0.622, and 0.822, respectively, against the unchanged full-model value of 0.937. Section 6 adds cluster-count estimates of (3, 2, 2, 2, 3) versus true counts (2, 2, 2, 2, 3). All pre-existing numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem statements, assumptions, losses, and metric definitions are unchanged, and Appendix A's proofs are identical. The added cluster indices in the warping equations clarify existing notation without supplying a new derivation or theoretical guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's principal novelty claim, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about unsupervised joint registration and clustering, theoretical guarantees, performance, robustness, and scalability. The additions support or explain these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific causal explanations for the discrete variant's poor Wave performance, attributes advantages over classical joint methods to particular NeuralFLoC components, and explains STFT degradation through high-frequency artifacts. It also discusses unknown-count applicability and the structural role of latent coordinates. The existing limitations remain unchanged; the stronger causal explanations lack dedicated diagnostic tests.

D1.justification: Section 6 newly discloses truncated-Fourier projection and reconstruction on a common grid for irregularly sampled inputs. Section 3.2 clarifies how latent coordinates initialize cluster-specific flows. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the retained experiments. Architecture specifications, optimization settings, and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gaffney and Smyth's joint probabilistic curve clustering and alignment reference and removes the Arbelaitz and Peng references associated with the earlier cluster-count suggestions. Discussion now explicitly positions performance against classical joint approaches, while the principal novelty claim remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized expansions explain the flow coordinates, comparison results, cluster-count selection, and irregular-input processing. The ablation paragraph moves before Table 1. The overall section organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains four rows, and added prose causes Algorithm 1, Figure 2, and other material to shift position. Existing figure content and captions are preserved, and the appendix pages are visually identical. There is no substantial graphical redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses the missing classical joint comparators and adds a useful control for the Fourier representation, strengthening empirical support for the retained method. The irregular-input preprocessing disclosure also improves reproducibility. These gains are limited by underspecified STFT and elbow-selection settings and stronger causal explanations without corresponding diagnostic evidence.
